source.title: Decoupling representation learning from reinforcement learning
source.venue: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 139:9870-9879

confidence_rationale: The most decision-relevant ML paper for REE's specific proposed architecture (frozen upstream encoder + separately-trained policy). Stooke et al. show a self-supervised temporal-contrastive encoder (ATC) can be trained separately from the policy and, held FROZEN, match or beat end-to-end RL -- but only because (a) the encoder objective was temporal-contrastive on control-relevant data and (b) a policy is STILL trained by RL on reward on top. Cuts both ways for REE: strongly supports the decoupled 'frozen e2 encoder + trainable policy head' design (V3-EXQ-737 / H1), while documenting the exact failure mode if the frozen features are not control-relevant (residual H2). Confidence 0.71 -- high relevance, but the two-edged verdict lowers directional confidence.
failure_signatures: Frozen-encoder success in ATC was CONDITIONAL on the encoder being trained with a temporal-contrastive objective on control-relevant observation streams. REE's e2 world-forward contrastive is temporally-contrastive in spirit, but if its features do not expose resource/hazard structure at the 5x5 local-view scale, a frozen-encoder + policy-head build can underperform -- the exact H2 residual.

ATC still trains the policy end-to-end by RL on reward. The paper is therefore ALSO evidence against REE's status quo: a decoupled encoder does NOT remove the need for a reward-trained policy; REE's bias-head is not a substitute for the RL-trained actor ATC always keeps.

Benchmarks are pixel-based DMControl/Atari with dense-ish shaping; REE's partially-observed implicit-reward forager is a harder control regime, so 'frozen encoder suffices' does not transfer automatically.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Representation learning can be decoupled from policy learning. An unsupervised temporal-contrastive task (Augmented Temporal Contrast, ATC) trains a convolutional encoder to associate observations a short time apart; training the encoder with ATC alone matches or outperforms end-to-end RL in most tested environments, and frozen ATC-pretrained encoders used inside RL agents outperform other unsupervised objectives. In all cases a policy is still learned by RL on reward on top of the (possibly frozen) encoder.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the closest ML precedent for REE's actual proposed fix under f_dominance_conversion_ceiling: keep the perceptual/prediction encoder (e2 world-forward contrastive) and add a separately-trained policy over it -- exactly V3-EXQ-737 (PPO policy head on frozen z_world). Stooke et al. give a positive existence proof that this decoupled shape CAN yield competent control, and that a frozen self-supervised encoder can even be sufficient. But the same paper is the evidence that REE's status quo is broken for a second reason: they ALWAYS train the policy by RL on reward -- a decoupled encoder never substitutes for the actor. REE's bias-head is not the ATC agent's RL-trained policy; it is the missing piece. So the paper simultaneously validates the H1 build design and warns that its success is gated on e2's features being control-relevant (H2).
mapping.mapping_caveat: ATC's frozen-encoder success depended on a temporal-contrastive objective over control-relevant pixel streams with (relatively) dense reward; REE's e2 is temporally-contrastive in spirit but its features may not expose resource/hazard structure under 5x5 partial observability and implicit reward. So the paper supports the DESIGN (decoupled encoder + RL policy) more strongly than it supports the PREDICTION that REE's specific frozen e2 will suffice -- hence evidence_direction=mixed.
mapping.source_context: Deep-RL-from-pixels benchmarks (DeepMind Control Suite, Atari); online RL plus a frozen-pretrained-encoder benchmark across several unsupervised representation objectives.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (ICML 2021 spotlight, widely cited, directly on the decoupled-representation question). Mapping fidelity 0.72: it is the closest available precedent for REE's exact frozen-encoder + trainable-policy design, but its verdict is two-edged (supports the design, warns on feature adequacy). Transfer risk 0.42 -- pixel DMControl/Atari with denser reward vs REE's partially-observed implicit-reward forager is a real regime gap, and the 'frozen encoder suffices' result is the part most at risk in transfer.
